1.title: Batch Ingestion, Schedules and Triggers
1.text: Welcome to Module one: Batch Ingestion, Schedules and Triggers. This module covers the task statement: perform data ingestion. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Read data from batch sources: Amazon S three, A W S Glue, Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce), A W S D M S (Database Migration Service), Amazon Redshift, A W S Lambda and Amazon AppFlow. Pick the configuration options that make a batch load correct, incremental and fast. Consume data A P I s safely: paging, authentication and retries. Start jobs on a schedule (EventBridge, Apache Airflow, cron) or by an event (S three Event Notifications, EventBridge). Let only the right network addresses reach a data source (allowlists). Handle throttling and rate limits with retries and backoff.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Loads Its First Data
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Loads Its First Data. Warehouse systems drop order files into a bucket every night. A Salesforce account holds customer records the analysts need. The billing database must be copied to the lake without slowing it down. A partner publishes fuel prices through a web A P I. Your job: pick the right tool for each source, then run each on time.

1.title: Batch or streaming
1.text: Batch or streaming. Batch: data arrives or is read in groups on a schedule or on an event (hourly files, a nightly export); results are minutes to hours old. Streaming: records are read one by one as they arrive (Module two); results are seconds old. Hourly, nightly, daily file, export point to batch; near real time, as it happens, continuous point to streaming.

1.title: Batch sources and tools
1.text: Batch sources and tools. The figure shows this: Batch ingestion paths: a SaaS application goes through Amazon AppFlow, a database through A W S D M S, files and objects through A W S Glue, Amazon E M R or Lambda, and a data warehouse through Amazon Redshift, all into the Amazon S three data lake.

1.title: Batch sources and tools, continued
1.text: Batch sources and tools, continued. Files already in Amazon S three. Service: A W S Glue, Amazon E M R, A W S Lambda. What to remember: Glue: serverless Spark E T L (extract, transform, load); E M R: Spark, Hive, Presto clusters or serverless; Lambda: small files and quick steps (fifteen-minute limit). Relational or NoSQL database (copy or keep in sync). Service: A W S D M S. What to remember: A managed replication server; full load, change data capture (C D C) or both; sources and targets can differ in engine. SaaS application (Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, ServiceNow, S A P and more). Service: Amazon AppFlow. What to remember: No code; flows run on demand, on a schedule or on an event; targets include S three and Redshift.

1.title: Batch sources and tools, continued
1.text: Batch sources and tools, continued. Amazon Redshift data. Service: Redshift unload to S three, copy from S three, federated query. What to remember: Glue and E M R can also read Redshift tables over J D B C (Java Database Connectivity). Bulk files from on premises. Service: A W S DataSync, A W S Transfer Family, A W S Snow Family. What to remember: DataSync: managed online transfer; Transfer Family: S F T P (Secure File Transfer Protocol), F T P S (File Transfer Protocol Secure) and F T P (File Transfer Protocol) into S three or E F S (Elastic File System); Snow Family: offline devices for very large or disconnected sites. Exam tip: The source decides the tool: SaaS to AppFlow, database to D M S, files in S three to Glue (serverless) or E M R (cluster control), S F T P partners to Transfer Family, on-premises file shares to DataSync.

1.title: AWS DMS in one page
1.text: A W S D M S in one page. D M S is a server in the cloud that runs replication software; you define a source endpoint, a target endpoint and a task. Migration types: full load (copy what exists), C D C (change data capture) (ongoing changes), full load plus C D C (copy, then keep in sync). Supports homogeneous (same engine) and heterogeneous (different engine) moves; S three is a common target for lake ingestion. Encrypts data at rest with A W S K M S (Key Management Service) and in flight with S S L (Secure Sockets Layer); a backup replication instance can take over on failure (Multi-A Z (Availability Zone)). Schema conversion is separate: D M S Schema Conversion or A W S S C T (Schema Conversion Tool) convert schemas; D M S moves the data (Module nine).

1.title: Amazon AppFlow in one page
1.text: Amazon AppFlow in one page. A fully managed integration service that moves data between SaaS applications and A W S services, without code. Triggers: on demand, on a schedule, or on an event (for example Salesforce platform events and change data capture events). Can map, filter, mask and validate fields, partition and aggregate the output files, and catalog the data in the A W S Glue Data Catalog. Data can travel privately over A W S PrivateLink instead of the internet. Custom connectors (a Python or Java S D K (software development kit)) reach sources that are not built in. Exam tip: "Ingest Salesforce data into S three or Redshift with the least code" is Amazon AppFlow. "Replicate a production database continuously" is A W S D M S with C D C.

1.title: Configuration Options for Batch Ingestion
1.text: Configuration Options for Batch Ingestion. Incremental load. Read only new or changed data: Glue job bookmarks, D M S C D C, a watermark (last timestamp or key). File format and size. Columnar (Parquet, O R C (Optimized Row Columnar)) and compressed files read faster and cost less; avoid millions of tiny files. Partitioning. Write to partitioned prefixes (for example by date) so queries scan less. Parallelism. More workers or D P U s (data processing unit) in Glue, more nodes in E M R, parallel load threads in D M S. Retries and idempotency. A re-run must not duplicate data: bookmarks, upserts, overwrite of a partition.

1.title: Configuration Options for Batch Ingestion, continued
1.text: Configuration Options for Batch Ingestion, continued. Batch window. Run when the source is quiet; keep the load inside the window.

1.title: Glue job bookmarks
1.text: Glue job bookmarks. A job bookmark is saved state that lets a Glue job skip data it has already processed on the next scheduled run. Options: Enable (track and update), Disable (the default: always read everything), Pause (read incrementally without updating the state). S three sources: supported formats include Jason, C S V, Avro, X M L, Parquet and O R C (Glue one point zero and later); a file is picked again if its last modified time changed. J D B C sources: a bookmark key, by default the primary key, which must increase or decrease sequentially with no gaps.

1.title: Glue job bookmarks, continued
1.text: Glue job bookmarks, continued. Bookmarks need a transformation ctx on each source and sink in the script and job.commit() at the end. Reset or rewind a bookmark to reprocess; Glue does not clean the target files, so write to a new output or de-duplicate. State is kept per job: deleting a job deletes its bookmark; changing the source path without changing transformation ctx makes the job skip files in the new path.

1.title: Loading Amazon Redshift from S3 (COPY)
1.text: Loading Amazon Redshift from S three (copy). Use copy, not many single inserts: it loads in parallel across the cluster's slices. Splittable inputs (uncompressed C S V, Parquet, O R C) are split automatically; Redshift splits files of one hundred twenty-eight megabytes or more. Not splittable (Jason, or C S V compressed with gzip): split into files of about one megabyte to one gigabyte after compression, and make the number of files a multiple of the number of slices. Load from one prefix with one copy (or a manifest file) so all files load together. Exam tip: "Load a large dataset into Redshift fast" to copy from S three, many similar-size files, compressed or columnar. "Process only new files each night" to Glue job bookmarks.

1.title: Consuming Data APIs
1.text: Consuming Data A P I s. Many sources (partners, SaaS, internal services) expose data through R E S T (representational state transfer) or other A P I s; a pipeline calls them from A W S Lambda, A W S Glue (Python jobs or custom connectors), Amazon AppFlow or a container. Pull patterns: pagination (follow next-page tokens), incremental requests (since a timestamp), authentication (keys and tokens kept in A W S Secrets Manager), retries with backoff on four twenty-nine and five hundred series. Rate limits are set by the provider; stay under them and spread calls over time. To publish your own data to other systems, put Amazon A P I Gateway in front of Lambda or a data store (Module three).

1.title: Consuming Data APIs, continued
1.text: Consuming Data A P I s, continued. A W S Data Exchange lets you find and subscribe to third-party datasets and receive them into S three. Exam tip: Secrets in A P I calls belong in Secrets Manager, never in the code or the job parameters in clear text.

1.title: Schedulers: Time-Based Starts
1.text: Schedulers: Time-Based Starts. Amazon EventBridge Scheduler. Use it for: A central, scalable schedule that calls two hundred seventy plus A W S services. Remember: cron and rate expressions, one-time schedules, time zones, flexible time windows, retries; the recommended way to schedule. EventBridge scheduled rules. Use it for: Older style: rule with a schedule. Remember: Legacy feature; no faster than every one minute. A W S Glue triggers. Use it for: Start jobs and crawlers. Remember: Types: on-demand, scheduled (cron), conditional (fire when other jobs or crawlers finish with a given status). Glue crawler schedule. Use it for: Keep the Data Catalog current. Remember: Time-based; a trigger can start at most two crawlers.

1.title: Schedulers: Time-Based Starts, continued
1.text: Schedulers: Time-Based Starts, continued. Apache Airflow (Amazon M W A A (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)). Use it for: Schedules inside D A G s (directed acyclic graph). Remember: The D A G's schedule interval starts the workflow (Module four).

1.title: EventBridge schedule expressions
1.text: EventBridge schedule expressions. rate(value unit): for example rate(five minutes); the unit is singular for one (rate(one hour)) and plural for more (rate(five hours)). cron(fields): six fields: minutes, hours, day-of-month, month, day-of-week, year; times are U T C unless a Scheduler time zone is set. You cannot set both day-of-month and day-of-week: use? in one of them. Example: cron(zero twelve? ) runs every day at twelve:zero U T C. Glue and crawlers also use cron: remember that day thirty-one does not exist in every month. Exam tip: A schedule starts a job at a time. If the job must start when data arrives, use an event trigger, not a schedule.

2.title: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens
2.text: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens. The figure shows this: S three event notification routing: a new object in the bucket can notify Amazon S N S, Amazon S Q S, A W S Lambda or Amazon EventBridge, and EventBridge can reach many more targets. Amazon S three Event Notifications publish events such as object created, object removed, restore, replication, lifecycle expiration and transition and tagging. Destinations: Amazon S N S (Simple Notification Service), Amazon S Q S (Simple Queue Service), A W S Lambda and Amazon EventBridge; prefix and suffix filters narrow the events to, for example, incoming or and.csv.

2.title: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens, continued
2.text: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens, continued. Delivery is at least once: usually in seconds, sometimes a minute or longer; make consumers idempotent. S Q S F I F O (first in, first out) queues are not a direct S three destination; route through EventBridge instead. Avoid loops: if the function writes to the same bucket that triggers it, it triggers itself; use two buckets or a prefix filter on the incoming path. Amazon EventBridge adds content-based filtering, many targets (Step Functions, Glue workflows, Lambda, S Q S, S N S and more), archive and replay, and partner and A W S service events.

2.title: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens, continued
2.text: Event Triggers: Start When Something Happens, continued. One simple reaction to new files (a Lambda). S three event notification to Lambda. Fan out to several consumers. S three to S N S ( to S Q S queues) or EventBridge. Buffer bursts and process at your pace. S three to S Q S to consumer. Rich routing, filtering, replay, many targets. S three to EventBridge. Start a Glue workflow or Step Functions run when a file lands. EventBridge rule with an S three event pattern. Exam tip: "Process each file as soon as it arrives" to S three event to Lambda, or EventBridge to Step Functions or Glue. "Every night at two A M" to a schedule.

2.title: Allowlists for Data Sources
2.text: Allowlists for Data Sources. Many sources (databases, partner A P I s, SaaS) accept connections only from known I P addresses; you give them a fixed address and they allow it. Glue, Lambda or an E C two (Elastic Compute Cloud) job inside a V P C (Virtual Private Cloud) reach the internet through a N A T (network address translation) gateway, which has a fixed Elastic I P address: give that address to the source's allowlist. For A W S D M S, the source database's security group or firewall must allow the replication instance (its private address in the same V P C, or its public address).

2.title: Allowlists for Data Sources, continued
2.text: Allowlists for Data Sources, continued. For databases in A W S, V P C security groups allow the security group of the job (a reference), which is better than an address list; use V P C endpoints and PrivateLink to avoid the internet. Amazon AppFlow can use A W S PrivateLink so the source never sees a public path. Exam tip: "The partner will accept traffic only from one I P address" to run the job in a V P C behind a N A T gateway with an Elastic I P and give the partner that I P.

2.title: Throttling and Rate Limits
2.text: Throttling and Rate Limits. Throttling means a service refuses requests above a limit: DynamoDB (ProvisionedThroughputExceededException, ThrottlingException), Amazon R D S (Relational Database Service) (connection and I O limits), Kinesis (per-shard throughput, Module two), A P I Gateway (H T T P four twenty-nine, default ten thousand requests per second with a five thousand-request burst per account per Region). Exponential backoff with jitter: wait a little longer after each failure (for example up to fifty milliseconds, then one hundred, then two hundred) with a random part so many clients do not retry together; A W S S D K s do this automatically.

2.title: Throttling and Rate Limits, continued
2.text: Throttling and Rate Limits, continued. Stop retrying after about a minute: if the request still fails, the problem is capacity, not rate, so raise the limit or provision more. Batch operations (BatchWriteItem) return unprocessed items: retry those with backoff. Fixes at the source of the limit: more capacity (provisioned throughput, on-demand mode, more shards, a bigger instance), spread the keys to avoid a hot partition, buffer with S Q S, batch writes, use R D S Proxy to pool connections.

2.title: Throttling and Rate Limits, continued
2.text: Throttling and Rate Limits, continued. The figure shows this: Exponential backoff with jitter: each retry waits about twice as long as the one before, with a random part, and retrying stops after about a minute. Exam tip: "Writes to DynamoDB are throttled during bursts" to on-demand mode or more provisioned capacity, retries with exponential backoff, a better partition key, and S Q S in front to smooth the load.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Source to tool: SaaS AppFlow; database D M S; S three files Glue or E M R or Lambda; S F T P Transfer Family; on-premises files DataSync. D M S: Full load, C D C, or both; heterogeneous moves; K M S at rest, S S L in flight. AppFlow: No code; on demand, schedule or event; mask, filter, partition; PrivateLink. Incremental: Glue job bookmarks (default disabled; S three by last-modified time; J D B C by sequential key), D M S C D C. Redshift load: copy from S three; splittable files split at one hundred twenty-eight megabytes. Schedule: EventBridge Scheduler (recommended), scheduled rules (legacy, at least one minute), Glue scheduled and conditional triggers, M W A A. cron: six fields (min, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week, year);? in one day field; U T C. Event: S three notifications to S N S, S Q S, Lambda, EventBridge; at least once; avoid same-bucket loops; F I F O via EventBridge.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Kestrel Freight wants customer records from Salesforce copied into Amazon S three every night with as little code as possible. Which service should the data engineer use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Amazon AppFlow is a managed, no-code integration service for SaaS sources and supports scheduled flows into S three. D M S is for databases, and Snow Family is for bulk offline transfer.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A nightly A W S Glue job reads C S V files from an S three prefix that gets new files every day. The job must process only files that arrived since the last run. What should the engineer enable? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Job bookmarks keep state between runs so the job skips data it has already processed. Workers add parallelism, conditional triggers chain jobs, and versioning keeps object versions.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A data engineer loads a very large set of gzip-compressed C S V files into Amazon Redshift. Which approach gives the fastest load? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. copy loads in parallel across slices; gzip-compressed C S V cannot be split automatically, so many similar-size files (about one megabyte to one gigabyte each) in a slice multiple load fastest.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. A pipeline must start a Lambda function within seconds of each new object arriving in a bucket. Which two statements describe a correct design? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and D. S three event notifications can invoke Lambda, and because delivery is at least once the consumer must handle duplicates. S three cannot send directly to an S Q S F I F O queue, polling is slower and wasteful, and writing to the triggering prefix creates a loop.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A partner A P I accepts requests only from one fixed I P address. The company's A W S Glue job runs in a V P C. What should the data engineer do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. A N A T gateway has a fixed Elastic I P address, so the partner can allowlist it. A whole Region range is not specific, and an I A M (Identity and Access Management) role does not change the source address.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. An ingestion job writes to Amazon DynamoDB and sometimes receives ProvisionedThroughputExceededException during bursts. What is the best first step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries, and the S D K s do it by default; if throttling continues the cause is capacity or a hot key, so adjust provisioned throughput, on-demand mode or the key design.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which statement about A W S D M S is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. D M S is a managed replication service that supports full load, C D C and both, and supports heterogeneous migrations. Schema conversion is a separate feature.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all seven answers. Question one: B. Question two: A. Question three: C. Question four: C and D. Question five: D. Question six: C. Question seven: A. In the next module, we continue the course.
